gaps.term: mu is not the number of central wires
gaps.quote: where $\mu$ is the number of central wires in one invocation
gaps.note: Wrong definition. In the paper the matrices are m x m with m=h^3=1000000 (line 656), while the number of central wires per invocation is c_b=100 (line 775). The size of the matrices is not the central-wire count; mu should be the matrix size (m).

The page never gives the value of mu for the explicit network (the paper has m=h^3=10^6, line 656, and uses m<2^20 at line 1333). With mu described as a number of central wires, the reader cannot check this bound.

gaps.quote: The outer two cost linear time.
gaps.note: The page gives no reason why D<-D-H and D<-H-D, with H and D multi-bit fields on tape, take linear time. The paper (line 1540) says these update the later field from the earlier one and cites its ordered-affine-streams lemma; the page neither states nor links this.

gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
gaps.note: The banks X, Y are sets of wire roles whose scalars are combined by gates. H and D are address fields of the array. In the paper the shear H<-H+D arises from the frame identity (sink minus source matrix equals the identity, lines 1495-1520) applied to every role stream, not by identifying D with X and H with Y. The page also blends the exchange of banks (X,Y) by the forward, inverse, forward schedule with the exchange of fields H, D done by the three updates, and gives no argument for the identification.

gaps.quote: by a restoration device the paper introduces as new
gaps.note: Misattributed. The paper (lines 354-360, 708-710) says its scratch schedule is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation of Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff and Speelman, Section 3, not a new device. Also, Lemma scalar-motifs gives (X,Y) -> (-Y,X), which is the exchange only in the bit construction.
